key_insight: A generalized swimming formula shows how anisotropic and odd viscosity affect microswimmer motion while preserving the scallop theorem in linearly viscous fluids.
engineering_relevance: The framework could guide microswimmer design and steering in chiral or anisotropic fluids, where strong shear can destabilize preferred orientations.
method: Apply the generalized Lorentz reciprocal theorem.
Establish Onsager–Casimir reciprocity for rigid-body resistance tensors.
Derive swimming velocities from prescribed surface motion and background flows.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical proofs and a spherical-swimmer analysis predicting shear-induced destabilization of bimodal chirotactic alignment, rather than experimental validation.
watch_item: Applicability is restricted to low-Reynolds-number, linearly viscous fluids; nonlinear rheology lies outside the stated framework.
paper_title: Swimming formula in a linearly viscous fluid with anisotropic and odd viscosity tensors at low Reynolds number
